title: Find an element in an array with break
description: Given an array of numbers, look for a specific element and stop as soon as you find it. Show the position or a not-found message.
hints: Declare boolean encontrado = false before the for
If nums[i] == buscado, set encontrado = true and print, then break
After the for loop, if !encontrado print 'Not found'
solutionExplanation: We use a boolean 'encontrado' to know whether the loop ended because of break or because it went through everything. When the number is found we print the position and break exits the loop immediately.

title: Filter negative numbers with continue
description: Iterate over an array with numbers (positive, negative and zero) and print only the positives using continue to skip the negatives and zeros.
hints: continue runs when the number is <= 0, skipping the printing
If the number is positive (> 0), it is printed
continue goes to the start of the next iteration without executing the rest of the code
solutionExplanation: In each iteration we check whether the number is <= 0; if so, continue skips the rest of the body (the printing) and goes directly to the next iteration. Only the positives reach the println.

title: Search and processing with labeled break
description: Use a labeled loop with a labeled break to look for a pair of numbers in a matrix that add up to a given target (similar to two sum). The labeled break exits both loops when the solution is found.
hints: Declare the label before the outer loop: busqueda:
Use break busqueda; (not break;) to exit both loops
Check only distinct pairs (j != k) in the same row
solutionExplanation: The label busqueda is placed before the first for loop. When the solution is found, break busqueda exits the 3 loops at once. Without the label, break would only exit the innermost loop. This is more efficient than a return because it allows later logic with the same structure.
